cards.claim: Training at lower resolution than test resolution improves final accuracy despite appearing to introduce a train-test mismatch
cards.conditions: ResNet-50, ImageNet, single-crop evaluation, training 120 epochs with SGD, testing at higher resolution
cards.effect: 77.1% top-1 accuracy when trained at 128×128 (vs 77.0% baseline at 224×224); training at 160×160 provides better accuracy than training at 224×224 while being 3x faster
cards.evidence: Empirical experimental results with ResNet-50 on ImageNet validation set
cards.quote: training at resolution 160 × 160 provides better results than the standard practice of training at resolution 224 × 224, while being more efficient. For instance, we obtain 77.1% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet with a ResNet-50 trained on 128 × 128 images, and 79.8% with one trained at 224 × 224.

cards.claim: Batch normalization adjustment is necessary and sufficient for adapting to resolution changes between training and test time
cards.conditions: ResNet-50, ImageNet, switching from train resolution to higher test resolution, fine-tuning on same training set
cards.effect: After BN fine-tuning, accuracy improves from 77.0% to 78.4% at test resolution 288×288 (1.4 pp gain); activation statistics closely resemble train-time statistics after BN adjustment
cards.evidence: Empirical measurement of activation distributions before/after fine-tuning; accuracy comparison with and without BN adaptation
cards.quote: A take-away from the distribution analysis is that the sparsity should be adapted. This requires at least to include the batch normalization that precedes the global pooling into the fine-tuning. In this way the batch statistics are adapted to the increased resolution... After fine-tuning the activation statistics closely resemble the train-time statistics.

cards.claim: Changing crop size at test time (without retraining) causes significant shifts in activation statistics that degrade performance without compensation
cards.conditions: ResNet-50 trained at 224×224, tested at varying resolutions (64, 128, 224, 288, 320 pixels)
cards.effect: At 64×64 test resolution, sparsity increases from 0.5% to 29.8% of activations being zero; distribution spreads (values >2 increase from 1.2% to 11.9%), but unadapted test at higher resolution still improves accuracy (78.4% at 288×288 vs 77.0% at 224×224)
cards.evidence: Measured cumulative density of activation vectors after average pooling layer on ImageNet validation set
cards.quote: Changing the size of the input crop strongly affects the activation statistics of this layer... At the default crop resolution of L_t = 224 pixels, the activation map is 7×7... At L_t = 64, the activation map is only 2×2: pooling only 0 values becomes more likely and activations are more sparse (the rate of 0's increases form 0.5% to 29.8%).

cards.claim: Lower training resolution reduces memory consumption and training time, enabling larger batch sizes
cards.conditions: ResNet-50 on ImageNet with 8 Tesla V100 GPUs, halving crop resolution from 224 to 112 or below
cards.effect: Halving crop resolution leads to 3x reduction in network evaluation speed and significant memory savings; reduces training time from 133.9h (native 224×224) to 111.8h with 128×128 training
cards.evidence: Training time measurements on hardware; computational complexity analysis
cards.quote: This significantly impacts the processing time: halving the crop resolution leads to a threefold reduction in the network evaluation speed and reduces significantly the memory consumption for a typical CNN, which is especially important for training on GPUs.

cards.claim: Fine-tuning only the final layers (batch norm + classifier) is sufficient to adapt from lower train resolution to higher test resolution
cards.conditions: ResNet-50 trained at 224×224 (or lower), adapted for test resolution 320×320, fine-tuning on same training set for 60 epochs with 10x smaller learning rate
cards.effect: Accuracy improves from 77.0% to 79.8% at test resolution 320×320 with minimal additional training (60 epoch fine-tune vs 120 epoch original training)
cards.evidence: Empirical comparison of fine-tuning only last layers vs full retraining; ablation of which layers need fine-tuning
cards.quote: we fine-tune on the same training set, after switching from L_t to L_s. Here we choose to restrict the fine-tuning to the very last layers of the network.
